**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 15, Verses 1–5**

**Explanation of the Words:**

**Alif-Lam-Ra** (الۤر): Allah knows best what He means by this. It is written as الۤر and is read: *Alif, Lam, Ra*.

**Those are the verses of the Book** (تلك آيات الكتاب): the verses composed of letters like these disjointed letters. "Those are the verses of the Book" means the Qur'an.

**Yawaddu** (يود): he loves and desires, wishing that he had been among the Muslims.

**Wa-yatamatta'u** (ويتمتعوا): that is, enjoying the pleasures and desires.

**Wa-yulhihim al-amal** (ويلههم الأمل): that is, through long life, attaining their aims and achieving worldly desires.

**Illa wa-laha kitabun ma'lum** (إلا ولها كتابٌ معلوم): that is, a fixed term for its destruction.

**Ma tasbiqu min ummatin ajalaha** (ما تسبق من أمة أجلها): that is, its appointed term cannot be advanced. (The word "min" here is extra, for emphasis.)

**Meaning of the Verses:**

Since the surah is Meccan, it deals with matters of belief, the greatest of which are monotheism (tawhid), prophethood, and resurrection. Allah's words, ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾: Allah knows best what He means by it. Among the benefits of these disjointed letters is to alert the listener and draw him in to what he hears of the recitation, since the disciples (of the Qur'an) used to prevent people from listening to it out of fear of being influenced by it. These openings, which they were not accustomed to in their speech, drew them to listen to what followed of the Qur'an. As for His words, ﴿Those are the verses of the Book﴾, it is permissible to say: the verses composed of such letters as الۤر, الۤمۤ, طسۤ, حمۤ, عۤسۤقۤ. ﴿Those are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur'an﴾. "Clear" (mubin) means clarifying truth and falsehood, guidance and misguidance.

Allah's words, ﴿Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish that they had been Muslims﴾: He, exalted is He, informs that a day will come, which is the Day of Resurrection, when the disbeliever sees the Muslims entering Paradise while he himself enters the Fire. On that day he will wish that he had been one of the Muslims. Allah may also bring about circumstances in this world, and matters, in which the disbeliever wishes that he had been a Muslim.

As for His words, ﴿Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves, and let hope distract them; but they will soon know﴾: that is, leave them, O our Messenger; leave the disbelievers to eat whatever food they wish, and to enjoy the desires and pleasures they have obtained, and let hope divert them from considering the outcome of their affair, since their concern is the length of their lives and the fulfilment of their aims. But they will soon know, when they are returned to Allah, their true Master, and what they used to invent will be lost to them, that in the world they were mistaken in turning away from the truth, from the call to truth, and from the true religion.

As for His words, ﴿And We never destroyed any town﴾: that is, any people of a town, with the punishment of annihilation and uprooting, ﴿except that it had a decreed term﴾: that is, it had a fixed term written in a Book, with its day and hour specified. As for His words, ﴿No nation can hasten its term, nor can it delay it﴾: that is, according to the Book of Decrees, a nation whose destruction Allah has decreed cannot have its destruction brought forward before its appointed time, nor can it be delayed from it even by an hour. In this there is a threat and warning to the people of Mecca, who were opposing the call to truth and the Messenger of truth, lest their town also has a decreed Book and a fixed term, while they are unaware.

**Guidance from the Verses:**

1. The noble Qur'an clarifies everything that is needed for human happiness and completeness.

2. A warning to the disbelievers and a caution against persisting in their disbelief and their opposition to Islam, for a day will come when they will wish that they had been Muslims.

3. Affirmation of the belief in divine decree and predestination (al-qada' wa al-qadar): nothing happens except that it was preceded by Allah's knowledge and recorded with Him in the Book of Decrees. Life and death, gain and loss, happiness and misery: all that has been, all that is, and all that will be has been preceded by Allah's knowledge and recorded in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 15, verses 6–11:

Explanation of the words:

Nazzala 'alayhi al-dhikr (“To whom the Reminder has been sent down”): i.e., the Noble Qur'an.

Law ma ta'tina bi'l-malaika (“Why do you not bring us the angels?”): i.e., why do you not bring us the angels to testify for you that you are a Prophet of Allah?

Wa ma kanu idhan munzarin (“And they would not then be given respite”): i.e., they would not be granted a reprieve; rather, the punishment would seize them immediately upon the descent of the angels.

Inna nahnu nazzalna al-dhikr (“Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder”): i.e., the Qur'an.

Fi shiya' al-awwalin (“among the sects of the former peoples”): i.e., among the groups and factions of the earlier peoples.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And they say: "O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, indeed you are a madman!"﴾ That is, the disbelievers who deny revelation and prophethood said this. "Indeed you are a madman" means: lacking reason, for otherwise you would not have claimed prophethood. In this saying of theirs there is a clear mockery of the Messenger ﷺ, and it is the fruit of the darkness of disbelief that is in their hearts. His words ﴿Why do you not bring us the angels, if you are of the truthful?﴾: here "law ma" carries the meaning of "hal" of urging, i.e., "Why do you not bring us the angels, that we may see them with our own eyes testifying to you that you are the Messenger of Allah, if you are of the truthful in your claim of prophethood and messengership? Then bring the angels to testify for you."

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿We do not send down the angels except with truth﴾: i.e., their descent is accompanied by truth. The angels do not descend except to establish the truth and nullify falsehood, not merely to satisfy people's whims and desires. Had the angels descended and they still did not believe, the punishment would have come upon them immediately. ﴿And they would not then be given respite﴾: i.e., they would not be granted a reprieve, but would be destroyed at once.

As for His words in verse [9]: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its guardian﴾: i.e., the Qur'an, and We are its guardian from being lost and from addition and subtraction, because it is Our proof upon Our creation until the Day of Resurrection. We sent down the Reminder as guidance, mercy, healing and light. They seek punishment, while Allah desires mercy. Although the Qur'an was brought down by the angels, and if the angels descended they would return to the heavens, nothing would remain to indicate the message except the Qur'an; but the people do not wish to believe. Nor are they alone in this disbelief and obstinacy; rather, nations and peoples before them were also sent messengers, and they denied and rejected them. This is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We certainly sent [messengers] before you among the sects of the former peoples﴾: i.e., among their groups and nations. ﴿And there never came to them a messenger except that they mocked him﴾, because the cause of the illness is one; therefore, O Messenger of Allah, do not despair and do not grieve, but be patient and wait, for Allah's promise of victory to you is true: ﴿Allah has decreed: "Surely I shall prevail, I and My messengers. Indeed Allah is Strong and Mighty."﴾ [al-Mujadila: 21].

Guidance from the verses:

1- Explanation of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ faced of mockery and ridicule from the polytheists.

2- A manifestation of Allah's mercy toward mankind: they seek the descent of punishment, while Allah sends down mercy.

3- Explanation of Allah's preservation of the Noble Qur'an from addition, subtraction and loss.

4- Explanation of Allah's sunnah concerning nations and peoples: whenever a messenger comes to them, challenging their familiar ways and calling them to a new good and guidance, they deny him and mock him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 15, verses 12–18:

Explanation of the words:

Kadhalika naslukuhu (Thus We cause it to enter): i.e., the denial of the Qur'an or of the Prophet ﷺ.

Wa qad khalat sunnat al-awwalin (And the way of the earlier peoples has already passed): i.e., the custom of the previous nations has passed on.

Fa-zallu fihi ya'rujun (So they kept ascending through it): i.e., they would climb up.

Innama sukkirat (They would only say: "Our sight has merely been dazzled"): i.e., it has been blocked, just as a river or a door is blocked (sukkira).

Fi al-sama' buruja (Constellations in the sky): i.e., stars in which the sun and the moon make their stations.

Shaytan rajim (An accursed devil): i.e., one stoned with shooting stars.

Shihab mubin (A clear flame): a star with which the devil is stoned, burning him, tearing him apart, or leaving him enfeebled (yukhbilu), i.e., corrupting him.

Meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues concerning those who denied the Prophet and demanded the descent of angels to bear witness to his prophethood, so that they would believe. Allah says: ﴿Thus do We cause it to enter into the hearts of the criminals﴾, i.e., the denial, into the hearts of the guilty among your people, just as We have caused it, according to Our custom, to enter the hearts of those who denied the messengers before you. So they do not believe in you nor in the Reminder that has been sent down to you. His saying: ﴿And the way of the earlier peoples has already passed﴾, i.e., it has gone by, and it is the punishment of those who denied the messengers and mocked them, because they will not believe until they see the painful punishment. His saying: ﴿And even if We opened for them a gate from the sky, and they continued to ascend through it﴾, i.e., the angels, or the deniers, ﴿through it﴾, i.e., through that gate, ﴿ascending﴾, i.e., climbing up throughout the day, going up and coming down, ﴿they would surely say: "Our sight has only been dazzled; rather, we are a people who have been bewitched."﴾ i.e., our sight has been prevented from true seeing, so we did not see the angels and did not see the sky, ﴿rather, we are a people bewitched﴾, so that we see things that have no reality. His saying: ﴿And We have certainly placed constellations in the sky﴾, i.e., stars which are stations for the sun and the moon, by which they travel, and by whose course the number of years and reckoning are known. His saying: ﴿And We have adorned it﴾, i.e., the sky with the stars, ﴿for the beholders﴾ among the people who look at it. His saying: ﴿And We have guarded it﴾, i.e., the lowest heaven, ﴿from every accursed devil﴾, i.e., one stoned and cursed. His saying: ﴿except one who steals a hearing﴾, i.e., except a rebellious devil who ascends to the sky to eavesdrop on the angels, so that he may bring the news down to his associates among the soothsayers of mankind, ﴿so a clear flame pursues him﴾ of fire, ﴿clear﴾, i.e., making its effect on the devil clear, either by enfeebling and corrupting him or by burning him. These verses, from His saying: ﴿And We have certainly placed constellations in the sky﴾ to the end of what comes in this long context, have as their purpose to demonstrate the power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy of Allah, all of which require the sending of the Messenger and the sending down of the Book to guide people to worship their Lord alone, a worship by which they perfect themselves and attain happiness in this world and the Hereafter; but the deniers do not know.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Explanation of Allah's custom regarding the stubborn deniers, which is that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment.

2- The demand of the criminal deniers for signs such as seeing the angels is meaningless, since the Qur'an is the greatest sign and they did not believe in it; therefore, even if a gate were opened for them from the sky and they continued to ascend through it, they would not believe.

3- Demonstration of the manifestations of Allah's power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy contained in these verses, beginning with His saying: ﴿And We have certainly placed constellations in the sky﴾ up to the twenty-seventh verse of this noble context.

Explanation of the words:

"And the earth — We have spread it out": i.e., We have stretched it out.

"And We cast into it firm mountains": i.e., immovable mountains, so that the earth does not shake.

"Measured": i.e., determined, of a known measure by Allah the Exalted.

"Means of livelihood": plural of ma'ishah, i.e., that by which a human being lives, such as foods.

"And those for whom you are not providers": such as slaves, bondswomen and beasts.

"And We do not send it down except in a known measure": i.e., the rain.

"And We sent the winds fertilising": i.e., they fertilise the clouds so that they become filled with water, just as the substance of pollen is carried from the male of the trees to its female.

"And you are not its storers": i.e., you do not possess its treasuries so that you could withhold it or give it to whom you wish.

"Those who go before you among you and those who come after": i.e., those among the children of Adam who have perished up to this day of yours, and those who come after, who are alive, and those who have not yet come into existence until the Day of Resurrection.

Meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues to mention the manifestations of Allah's power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy, which are the grounds for believing in Him, worshipping Him, affirming His oneness, and drawing near to Him by doing what He loves and abstaining from what displeases Him. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the earth — We have spread it out﴾, i.e., stretched it out, ﴿and cast into it firm mountains﴾, i.e., firm mountains that stabilise the earth so that it does not move or sway with its inhabitants and they perish, ﴿and We caused to grow in it of every thing a measured quantity﴾, i.e., determined, of a known measure by Allah the Exalted. His saying: ﴿And We have made for you therein means of livelihood﴾, by which you live upon it, and these are kinds of grains, fruits and other things; His saying: ﴿and those for whom you are not providers﴾, but Allah the Exalted is the One who provides for them and for you, from among the slaves, bondswomen and beasts. His saying: ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasuries, and We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾, i.e., there is nothing beneficial to mankind, which they need for the sustenance of their lives, except that with Allah are its treasuries, and among these is rain; yet He sends it down in a measure known according to the needs of creatures and what their welfare depends upon. This is like His saying: ﴿In whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent﴾ [al-Mulk: 1], and like His saying: ﴿And if Allah had extended provision for His servants, they would have transgressed upon the earth, but He sends down in measure what He wills. Indeed He is of His servants Acquainted and Seeing﴾ [ash-Shura: 27]. His saying: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilising﴾, i.e., they fertilise the clouds so that they become filled with water, ﴿then We sent down from the sky water﴾ by Our power and management, ﴿and We gave it to you to drink, and you are not its storers﴾, i.e., you do not possess its treasuries so that you could withhold it or give it to whom you wish; rather Allah the Exalted is the Owner of that, so He sends it down upon the land of one people and withholds it from others. His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the inheritor﴾, and ﴿We have certainly known those who go before you among you﴾, i.e., those who died from the time of Adam, ﴿and We have certainly known those who come later﴾, of those who are alive, and those who have not yet come into existence but will come into existence and die until the Day of Resurrection. All of them are known to Allah, and none other knows them; therefore He alone deserves worship, and none other deserves it. His saying: ﴿And indeed, your Lord﴾, O Messenger, ﴿He will gather them﴾, i.e., to Him on the Day of Resurrection, to call them to account and recompense them. This depends upon power, wisdom and knowledge: the One who gave them life and then caused them to die is able to bring them back to life a second time; the One who knew them before their creation and knows them after their creation is able to gather them; and the Wise, who places everything in its proper place, did not create them in vain, but created them to test them, then to call them to account and recompense them. Indeed, He is the Wise, the All-Knowing.

1- Explanation of the manifestations of Allah's power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy, which are evident in the following:
a- The creation of the earth, its spreading out, and the casting of mountains into it; the sending of winds as fertilisers of the clouds.

3- Affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 15, verse 26–33:

Explanation of the words:

"And We created man": i.e., Adam (peace be upon him).

"from clay of black mud, molded": i.e., dry clay that produces a ringing sound (ṣalṣāl), from black mud (ḥama'), i.e., black mud that has changed.

"And the jinn We created before from the fire of the simoom": a fire with no smoke that penetrates the pores, and the pores are the openings of the human skin.

"So when I have proportioned him": i.e., I have completed his creation.

"Then fall down to him in prostration": i.e., bow down to him in prostration.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to mention the manifestations of God's power, knowledge, wisdom and mercy. The Almighty's saying: ﴿And We did certainly create man﴾, i.e., Adam, ﴿from clay﴾, i.e., dry clay that produces a ringing sound. ﴿of black mud, molded﴾, i.e., black mud whose smell has changed; this is one of the manifestations of power and knowledge. His saying: ﴿And the jinn We created before from the fire of the simoom﴾: before the creation of Adam; the jinn is the father of the jinn. ﴿From the fire of the simoom﴾, and the fire of the simoom is a fire without smoke that penetrates the pores of the body... His saying ﴿And when your Lord said﴾, i.e., mention, O Our Messenger, when your Lord said to the angels: prostrate to Adam, i.e., a prostration of greeting and honor, not a prostration of worship to Adam, since the one worshipped is the commander who is obeyed, and He is God Most High. So they prostrated, ﴿except Iblis; he refused﴾, i.e., he refused to be among those prostrating. His saying: ﴿He said, "O Iblis, what is [the matter] with you that you are not among those who prostrate?"﴾, i.e., what has happened to you that you refused to be among those who prostrate from among the angels? So the accursed one revealed the reason for his refusal, which is his envy of Adam and his arrogance, and he said, ﴿I would not prostrate to a human whom You created from clay, from black mud, molded.﴾ In the following verses is God Most High's answer and His rebuttal of him.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Explanation of the origin of human creation, which is clay, and of the jinn, which is a flame of fire.

2- The virtue of prostration, since the Most High commanded the angels to it, and they all prostrated except Iblis.

3- Condemnation of envy, and that it is the worst of sins and the most harmful.

4- Condemnation of arrogance, and that it is an obstacle that prevents its possessor from perfection in this world and happiness in the Hereafter.

5- The superiority of clay over fire, because Adam was created from clay and Iblis was created from fire.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 15, verses 34–44:

Explanation of the words:

"Qala fakhruj minha" (He said: "Get out of it"): i.e., out of Paradise.

"Fa innaka rajim" (Indeed, you are accursed): i.e., stoned, expelled, cursed.

"Ila yawm al-waqt al-ma'lum" (Until the Day of the Appointed Time): i.e., the time of the First Blast, when all creation will die.

"Bima aghwaytani" (Because You have led me astray): i.e., because of your misguiding me, that is, your leading me into error and corruption.

"Al-mukhlisin" (the sincere ones): i.e., those whom You have chosen for Your obedience, for my scheme does not affect them.

"Hadha sirat 'alayya mustaqim" (This is a straight path to Me): i.e., this is a straight path that leads to Me, and it is incumbent upon me to observe and preserve it.

"Laha sab'at abwab" (It has seven gates): i.e., the gates of its seven levels, which are Jahannam, then Laza, then al-Huṭama, then al-Sa'ir, then Saqar, then al-Jahim, then al-Hawiya.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Most High, ﴿So get out of it﴾, are a response to the statement of Iblis, ﴿I will never prostrate to a human whom You created from clay﴾ [al-Hijr: 33]. So: get out of it, i.e., out of Paradise, ﴿for indeed, you are accursed﴾, i.e., stoned, expelled, distanced, ﴿and indeed, upon you is the curse﴾, i.e., My wrath and My removal of you from the heavens, ﴿until the Day of Judgment﴾, i.e., until the Day of Resurrection, which is the Day of Recompense. The accursed one then said what Allah the Most High reported of him: ﴿My Lord, give me respite﴾, i.e., grant me respite and do not cause me to die, ﴿until the Day they are resurrected﴾. The Lord, the Most High, responded with His words: ﴿Indeed, you are of those given respite﴾, i.e., those granted reprieve, ﴿until the Day of the Appointed Time﴾, which is the annihilation of the children of Adam, when none of them remains, and that is at the First Blast. When the accursed one heard what the Lord, the Most High, had decreed against him, he said what Allah reported of him in His words: ﴿My Lord, because You have led me astray﴾, i.e., because of Your leading me astray, ﴿I will make [evil] attractive to them on earth﴾, i.e., disbelief, polytheism and major sins, ﴿and I will mislead them all﴾, i.e., I will lead them astray entirely, ﴿except among them Your chosen servants, the sincere ones﴾. The accursed one thus excepted those whom Allah the Most High has chosen for His obedience and honored with His guardianship, those whom anger does not overpower, and over whom desire and whim have no control. And the words of the Most High, ﴿He said, "This is a straight path to Me"﴾, i.e., this is a straight path leading to Me that I observe and preserve, and it is ﴿indeed, My servants, over them you have no authority, except those who follow you of the misguided﴾. ﴿And indeed, Jahannam﴾ is the promised place for you and for your followers among the misguided, all of them, ﴿it has seven gates﴾, for it consists of seven levels, each level having a gate above it through which the people of that level enter. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿For every gate there is a designated portion of them﴾, i.e., a specified share. Its levels are: Jahannam, Laza, al-Huṭama, al-Sa'ir, Saqar, al-Jahim, al-Hawiya.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The deprivation of Iblis from repentance, due to the continuation of Allah's wrath upon him until the Day of Resurrection.

2- Allah responded to the request of the most evil of His creation, Iblis; thus it is permissible for Allah to answer the supplication of a disbeliever for a wisdom that Allah intends.

3- The most effective weapon with which Iblis misleads the children of Adam is making things attractive, even if they are ugly and repulsive; through his whisperings he makes them appear as beautiful adornments until the person approaches them.

4- The infallibility of the messengers and Allah's protection of the saints so that they are not defiled by the filth of sins.

5- The path of Allah is straight, leading to Allah the Most High, which people follow until they reach Allah, the Glorified, Who then holds them to account and recompenses them for their deeds: good with good and evil with evil.

7- Clarification that Jahannam has levels, one above another, and each level has its gate above it through which only the people of that level enter.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 15, verses 45–56:**

**Explanation of the words:**

**Inna al-muttaqin** (Indeed the God-conscious): those who feared their Lord, worshipped Him alone, and performed the acts of worship He prescribed for them.

**Wa naza'na ma fi sudurihim min ghill** (And We removed whatever rancour was in their breasts): i.e., hatred, envy, enmity, and malice.

**Ala sururin mutaqabilin** (On couches facing one another): i.e., they look at one another while they sit, and when they turn away, the couches turn them around so that no one sees the back of another.

**La yamassuhum fiha nasabun** (No fatigue will touch them therein): i.e., weariness.

**Al-'adhab al-alim** (The painful punishment): i.e., that which causes great pain.

**Dayf Ibrahim** (the guests of Abraham): they were angels who came down to him while on their way to the people of Lot to destroy them. Among them was Jibril, and they appeared in the form of young men.

**Inna minkum wajilun** (Indeed, we are apprehensive of you): i.e., afraid. This was because they refused to eat.

**Bighulamin alim** (of a knowledgeable boy): i.e., a son with much knowledge. He was Isaac, peace be upon him.

**Fa bima tubashirun** (Then what is it that you give good news of?): i.e., he expressed wonder at their good news of a son despite his old age.

**Min al-qanitin** (of those who despair): i.e., those who have lost hope.

**Meaning of the verses:**

When Allah mentioned the reward for those who followed the misguided Iblis, it was fitting to mention the reward of the servants of the Most Merciful, the people of God-consciousness and faith. So Allah, the Exalted, said, informing about what He has prepared for them of enduring bliss: ﴿Indeed, the God-conscious will be in gardens and springs﴾, i.e., those who avoid polytheism and sins. ﴿It will be said to them: Enter them in peace, secure﴾, i.e., while you are accompanied by peace and safe from fear and terror. His saying ﴿And We will remove whatever rancour is in their breasts﴾ means Allah does not leave in the breasts of the people of Paradise anything that would spoil its bliss or cloud its purity, such as spite, envy, enmity, or hostility.

His saying ﴿as brothers on couches facing one another﴾: since He purified their hearts of whatever would spoil or cloud them, they became brothers in love for one another, gathered in one assembly, sitting on couches facing each other face to face. When they wish to go to their palaces, the couches turn them around, so none of them sees the back of his brother.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿No fatigue will touch them therein, nor will they be removed from it﴾ contains the report of two blessings: the blessing of everlasting rest, since there is no weariness or toil in Paradise, and the blessing of permanence and eternity therein, since they will never be removed from it. In this is a confirmation of the belief in resurrection and recompense in the most eloquent and clear expression.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾, i.e., inform, O Our Messenger, Our servants who believe and affirm Our oneness, that their Lord forgives them if they disobey Him and then repent of their disobedience, and is merciful to them so He will not punish them. ﴿And that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾: and inform them also that My punishment is the painful punishment, so let them beware of disobeying Me by associating partners with Me or by violating My commands and committing what I have forbidden.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And inform them about the guests of Abraham, when they entered upon him and said, "Peace." He said, "Indeed, we are apprehensive of you."﴾ i.e., they greeted him with peace, and he returned their greeting and presented them the hospitality due to guests, which was a roasted calf, as mentioned in Hud. He offered them food, but they refused. Here he said, ﴿Indeed, we are apprehensive of you﴾, i.e., afraid. They were Jibril, Mikail, and Israfil in the form of handsome young men. When he informed them of his fear of them, because the custom is that when a person's guest does not eat his food, this indicates that he intends harm.

﴿They said, "Do not fear.  Indeed, we give you good news of a knowledgeable boy."﴾ i.e., do not be afraid; we give you news of a son with much knowledge. Abraham responded, stating what Allah related about him in His saying: ﴿He said, "Do you give me good news although old age has touched me? Then what is it you give good news of?"﴾ i.e., is this news of a child despite my old age, or is it something strange? When he wondered at the good news and signs of doubt and hesitation about the truth of the report appeared on him, they said to him: ﴿We have given you good news in truth, so do not be of those who despair.﴾ i.e., those who have lost hope. Here he replied to them, denying despair from himself, because despair is prohibited. ﴿And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except the astray?﴾ i.e., the disbelievers in Allah's power and mercy, because of their ignorance of their Lord and His attributes, which are manifest in His mercy toward them and His favour upon them.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Affirmation of the bliss of Paradise, that its bliss is both physical and spiritual together, and it is everlasting forever.
2. The purity of Paradise's bliss from everything that would spoil or cloud it.
3. Allah's promise of forgiveness to those among the believers and the God-conscious who monotheize Him and repent.
4. His warning to the people of disobedience if they do not repent to Him before their death.
5. The legitimacy of hospitality, and that it is among the forms of righteousness and generosity.
6. The prohibition of despair and hopelessness from the mercy of Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 15, verses 57–66:

Explanation of the words:

"He said, 'What then is your business?'" (qala fa-ma khatbukum): that is, what is your matter?

"To a people who are criminals" (ila qawmin mujrimin): they are the people of Lot, peace be upon him.

"Indeed, We will save them all" (inna lamunajjuhum ajma'in): that is, because of their faith and righteous deeds.

"Among those who remain behind" (al-ghabirin): that is, those who remain in the punishment.

"People unknown" (qawm munkarun): that is, I do not know you.

"With that about which they used to doubt" (bima kanu fihi yamtarun): that is, with the punishment about whose occurrence they used to be in doubt.

"Wherever you are commanded" (haythu tu'marun): that is, to al-Sham (Greater Syria), where they were commanded to go out.

"And We decreed that matter to him" (wa qadayna ilayhi dhalika al-amr): that is, We informed Lot of that matter, and We revealed to him that the last remnant of these people would be cut off at dawn.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to speak of Abraham's guests. Here he asked them, as Allah the Exalted had reported about him, saying: ﴿He said, "What then is your business, O messengers?"﴾ That is, what is your matter, O messengers from Allah, since they were His angels? ﴿They said, "Indeed, we have been sent to a people who are criminals"﴾ that is, against themselves and against others, and they are the people of Lot, may Allah curse them. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿except the family of Lot﴾ means his household and the believers with him. ﴿Indeed, We will save them all, except his wife; We have decreed that she will be among those who remain behind﴾ that is, We have decreed it, that is, Allah has decided and ordained her destruction among those who will be destroyed, because she is a disbeliever like them. Here the conversation with Abraham ended, and they moved on to the city of Lot, peace be upon him. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when the messengers came to the family of Lot﴾ that is, they reached them and entered upon them in the house. Lot, peace be upon him, said to them: ﴿"Indeed, you are a people unknown"﴾ that is, I do not know you. They answered him saying: "We are messengers of your Lord; we have come to you with that about which your people used to doubt," that is, their immediate punishment, as recompense for their disbelief and criminality. ﴿And We have brought you the truth﴾ the certain reality about which there is no doubt, ﴿and indeed, we are truthful﴾ in what We have told you, which is the punishment of his criminal people. Accordingly: ﴿So travel with your family in the darkness of the night﴾ that is, set out with them during part of the night, ﴿and follow behind them﴾ that is, walk behind them while they are ahead of you, ﴿and let none of you look back﴾ by looking behind him, that is, so that he does not see what would grieve him when the punishment descends upon the criminals. And His saying: ﴿and proceed to where you are commanded﴾ that is, where your Lord commands you; they had been commanded to go to al-Sham. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We decreed that matter to him: that the last remnant of these would be cut off by morning﴾ that is, We informed Lot of that matter and revealed to him that these people would be destroyed to the last one in the early morning, meaning that as soon as the morning dawns, the earth will be overturned with them and they will be destroyed to the last one.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Condemnation of criminality and explanation of the punishment of criminals.

2- Lineage has no value, nor does marriage relation, nor is kinship of any account when disbelief and criminality separate lineages and relatives. Lot's wife perished with those who perished, and it did not benefit her that she was the wife of a prophet and messenger, peace be upon him.

3- The permissibility of travelling by night to cover long distances.

4- The permissibility of a leader or elder of the people walking behind the army and the caravan to check on their conditions and to learn of any who lag behind for some reason; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do likewise.

5- The disliking of showing compassion toward the wrongdoers who are destroyed, based on His saying: "and let none of you look back," meaning: in his heart.

**Explanation of the Words:**

﴿وجاء أهل المدينة يستبشرون﴾: That is, the city of Sodom (Sadum), rejoicing at committing the indecency.

﴿واتقوا الله ولا تخزون﴾: That is, do not humiliate me by violating the sanctity of my guest.

﴿أولم ننهك عن العالمين﴾: That is, from giving them refuge and hosting them.

﴿لفي سكرتهم يعمهون﴾: That is, in their misguidance and their intense lust, which removed their reason, wandering about aimlessly.

﴿مشرقين﴾: That is, at the time of sunrise.

﴿من سجيل﴾: That is, clay baked by fire.

﴿لآيات للمتوسمين﴾: That is, for those who look and take heed.

﴿لبسبيل مقيم﴾: That is, the road of Quraysh to al-Sham (Syria) is lasting, permanent and established.

﴿أصحاب الأيكة﴾: That is, the people of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him), and al-Ayka (the thicket) is a dense growth of trees near Madyan.

﴿وإنهما لبإمام مبين﴾: That is, the people of Lut and the companions of the thicket are upon a clear and evident road.

**Meaning of the Verses:**

The context continues with Lut (peace be upon him) and his guests from among the angels on one side, and the people of Lut on the other. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the people of the city came, rejoicing﴾. That is, the people of the city of Sodom, whose inhabitants were followers of Lut, were joyful and delighted, hoping to commit the indecency. Lut said to them what Allah the Exalted reported: ﴿Indeed, these are my guests, so do not disgrace me﴾. That is, do not disgrace me in regard to them by your demand for indecency. ﴿And fear Allah﴾, that is, be mindful of Him, ﴿and do not humiliate me﴾, that is, do not degrade or belittle me.

They replied with what Allah the Exalted reported about them: ﴿Did we not forbid you from the people of the worlds?﴾ That is, do you say what you say without mentioning that we forbade you from hosting or protecting any of the people? Lut (peace be upon him) answered them with what Allah the Exalted reported of him: ﴿He said, "These are my daughters, if you are going to act"﴾. That is, these are my daughters, so marry them, if you are going to do what I command you or guide you to.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿By your life, [O Muhammad], indeed they were, in their intoxication, wandering blindly﴾. That is, by your life, O our Messenger, indeed they, the people of Lut, were in their misguidance, which had taken away their reason, so they sank to a level lower than that of animals, ﴿wandering blindly﴾, that is, bewildered and wandering. ﴿So the shriek seized them at sunrise﴾, that is, the shriek of Jibril (peace be upon him) at the rising of the sun. Allah says: ﴿And We rained upon them﴾ in addition to that ﴿stones of baked clay﴾, that is, clay baked by fire.

Allah says: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those who look and take heed﴾. That is, in what has been mentioned of the destruction of entire cities with their inhabitants are signs, lessons and admonitions for the ones who take heed, that is, those who look with reflection and contemplation so as to know things by their marks and signs. Allah says: ﴿And indeed, they are on an established road﴾. That is, these ruined towns lie on a road that is firm and enduring, which the people of Makkah pass along on their journeys to al-Sham. Allah says: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for the believers﴾. That is, a lesson for the believers, so that they do not approach what Allah has forbidden and do not commit His sins.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And indeed, the companions of the thicket were wrongdoers﴾. This is a brief allusion to the story of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) with his people, the companions of the thicket. Al-Ayka is a thick, intertwined growth of trees. Their dwellings were there, and they were polytheists, and this is the wrongdoing in His words, ﴿they were wrongdoers﴾, because they wronged themselves by worshipping other than Allah the Exalted. Allah says: ﴿So We took retribution from them﴾, that is, We destroyed them with a severe heat on the Day of the Shade (al-Zullah). Their story will come in Surat al-Shu'ara'. There Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them; indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous day﴾.

His words: ﴿And indeed, they are on a clear highway﴾. Al-Imam (the highway) is the road, because people walk along it and it lies before them. Mubin means clear and evident. The pronoun in "and indeed they" refers to the people of Lut and the people of Shu'ayb, who are the companions of the thicket, not the people of Madyan, because he was sent to the companions of the thicket and to the people of Madyan. The road is the road of Quraysh to al-Sham. The purpose of mentioning this is to admonish Quraysh and remind them. Will they then take heed and remember?

**Lessons from the Verses:**

Among the lessons of the verses:

1- Explanation of the destruction of the people of Lut.

2- Condemnation of the indecency, and that the most abominable indecency known to humanity is intercourse with males.

3- Explanation of Lut's (peace be upon him) defence of his guests, to the point of offering them his daughters.

4- The honour of the Prophet (ﷺ), in that Allah the Exalted swore by his life in His words, ﴿By your life﴾.

5- Encouragement to contemplative reflection, to take heed and to discern by signs, for it is more beneficial to the human intellect.

6- Explanation of Allah the Exalted's retribution against the wrongdoers, as a lesson and admonition.

7- Confirmation of the prophethood of the Messenger (ﷺ), since such reports could only come from divine revelation.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 15, verses 80–88:

Explanation of the words:

Ashab al-Hijr (the People of al-Hijr): they are the people of Salih, and their dwellings were between Madinah (the City of the Prophet) and al-Sham (Greater Syria).

Wa-atayna-hum ayatina (And We gave them Our signs): that is, in the she-camel, which was the greatest sign.

Ma aghna 'anhum ma kanu yaksibun (What they used to earn did not avail them): such as building fortresses and gathering wealth.

Al-Safh al-Jamil (the gracious forgiveness): that is, turn away from them with a turning-away in which there is no anxiety, and this was before the command to fight them.

Sab'an min al-mathani (seven of the oft-repeated): these are the seven verses of Surat al-Fatihah.

Azwajan minhum (pairs of them): that is, kinds of disbelievers.

Wakhfid janahaka (and lower your wing): that is, be gentle toward the believers.

Meaning of the verses:

Ashab al-Hijr (the People of al-Hijr): they are the people of Salih, and their dwellings were between Madinah (the City of the Prophet) and al-Sham (Greater Syria).

Wa-atayna-hum ayatina (And We gave them Our signs): that is, in the she-camel, which was the greatest sign.

Ma aghna 'anhum ma kanu yaksibun (What they used to earn did not avail them): such as building fortresses and gathering wealth.

Al-Safh al-Jamil (the gracious forgiveness): that is, turn away from them with a turning-away in which there is no anxiety, and this was before the command to fight them.

Sab'an min al-mathani (seven of the oft-repeated): these are the seven verses of Surat al-Fatihah.

Azwajan minhum (pairs of them): that is, kinds of disbelievers.

Wakhfid janahaka (and lower your wing): that is, be gentle toward the believers.

Meaning of the verses:

This is the beginning of a brief account of another story, the story of the People of al-Hijr, who were Thamud, the people of Salih. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the people of al-Hijr denied the messengers﴾. In this there is an admonition to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), since his people, the people of Makkah, denied him; so let him be patient with their denial, for peoples before them had denied. Allah says ﴿the messengers﴾, although they denied only Salih, on the basis that whoever denies one messenger has denied all the messengers, because the call of the messengers is one: that Allah alone be worshipped, by that which He prescribed for the perfection and happiness of man in both states. As for His saying ﴿And We gave them Our signs, but they turned away from them﴾, the signs granted in the she-camel included that it came out of a rock, that it drank the water of the town one day, and that it stood in front of every house so that its people could milk from it what they wished. Their turning away from them was their failure to believe and their failure to repent to Allah the Exalted, after He had given them what they asked for in the way of signs. As for His saying ﴿And they used to hew out houses from the mountains﴾, that is, they would carve out by hewing dwellings inside the mountains, living in them in winter, safe from them collapsing upon them because of their strength, and from cold or heat reaching them, because of the protection they afforded. As for His saying, the Exalted, ﴿So the Shout seized them at morning-time﴾, that was the shout of the fourth day, which was a Saturday, and they all perished. ﴿Then what they used to earn did not avail them﴾ of wealth, equipment, and building fortresses. Rather they perished, and none of them was saved except those who believed and did righteous deeds, for Allah the Exalted saved them along with His Prophet Salih, peace be upon him. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾, that is, only so that I be remembered and thanked; therefore whoever disbelieves in Me, not remembering Me, and disobeys Me, not thanking Me, I will destroy him, for I did not create this great creation in play, falsehood, or futility. As for His saying: ﴿And indeed the Hour is coming﴾, that is, certainly, without doubt, and there each will be recompensed for what he earned. So do not grieve over your people or be distressed by them, for their recompense is binding and coming, without fail. So be patient and forgive them; this is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted, ﴿So forgive with gracious forgiveness﴾, that is, forgiveness with which there is no anxiety. As for His saying ﴿Indeed your Lord is the All-Creator, the All-Knowing﴾: He created everything and knows what He created; despite the multitude of creatures, He knows their intentions, their deeds, and their states, and nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him. He will restore them as He originated them, will reckon with them, and will recompense them for what they earned. This is something that helps the Messenger (ﷺ) to be patient and steadfast in his call until Allah the Exalted grants it victory at the time He has appointed for it.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated and the Great Quran﴾: that is, We gave you the Surah of al-Fatihah, the Mother of the Quran, and We gave you the Great Quran, which is a great good whose worth cannot be measured. Therefore ﴿do not extend your eyes﴾ longingly ﴿toward what We have given to pairs of them﴾, that is, kinds of the men of Quraysh. What We have given you is better than what they have of wealth and of the condition in which they enjoy savoury food and drink. As for His saying: ﴿And do not grieve over them﴾ if they do not believe in you or follow you in what you have brought, for their affair is with Allah the Exalted. He commanded him to lower his side for his believing Companions, so He said: ﴿And lower your wing to the believers﴾. Allah's guardianship of you is sufficient for you; so leave the deniers, the possessors of blessings, keep company with the believers, be gentle toward them, and be kind to them, for the good is in them, and not in those wealthy, affluent, disbelieving, wicked men.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- When Allah wills the destruction of a nation, its material strength avails it nothing.

2- Allah did not create creation in vain; rather He created it to be worshipped through remembrance and gratitude. Whoever worships Him is saved, and whoever turns away from His remembrance and abandons His worship, He will make him taste the punishment of disgrace in this world and the Hereafter, or in the Hereafter, which is more severe and more disgraceful.

3- Clarification that the gracious forgiveness is that with which there is no anxiety.

4- Clarification that whoever has been given the Quran has not been given anyone's like of good, ever.

5- The virtue of al-Fatihah, since it is the seven oft-repeated.

6- Those who call to Allah must not turn their attention to what is in people's hands of wealth and goods, for what Allah has given them of faith, knowledge, and piety is better than what He has given those others of wealth and goods.

7- Recommendation of gentleness toward the believers, showing them kindness and mercy.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 15, verses 89–99:**

**Explanation of the words:**

**An-nadhir al-mubin:** *al-mubin* means clear in warning.

**ʿAla al-muqtasimin:** That is, those who divided God's Book, saying of it that it is poetry, saying that it is sorcery, and saying that it is soothsaying.

**Ja'alu al-Qur'ana ʿidin** (*ʿidin*, plural of *ʿiḍah*, meaning a piece or a part of a thing): They are the dividers of the Qur'an, who made it into fragments.

**Fa-isda' bima tu'mar:** That is, proclaim it openly and present it as your Lord has commanded you.

**Yadiqu sadruka bima yaqulun:** That is, because of their mockery of you and their denial of you.

**Hatta ya'tiyaka al-yaqin:** That is, death. In other words, continue worshipping your Lord until you die.

**Meaning of the verses:**

The context continues with guidance to the Messenger ﷺ and instruction on how he should conduct himself. God commands him, saying: ﴿And say, "I am indeed the clear warner"﴾, meaning: declare to your people that you are a clear warner to them, that the punishment of God will descend upon them if they persist in polytheism, obstinacy and disbelief. His saying ﴿As We sent down upon the dividers, those who made the Qur'an into fragments﴾ means: I warn you of a punishment like the one God sent down, and sends down, upon the dividers, those who divided the Torah and the Gospel, believing in some of it and disbelieving in some of it. They are the Jews and the Christians. The dividers also include those who conspired to raid Salih by night, whom God punished for their scheme. The dividers further include those who made the Qur'an into fragments, that is, parts, saying of it that it is poetry, sorcery and soothsaying. And the dividers include those who divided the roads of Makkah and set them up as checkpoints, barring from the path of God everyone who came seeking Islam. All of these are dividers, and the punishment and vengeance of God befell them.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely call them all to account for what they used to do﴾. The Almighty, Blessed and Exalted, swears to His Messenger that He will surely question them on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to do, and will recompense them for it. Therefore, let their affair not distress you, and be patient with their harm.

His saying: ﴿So proclaim what you are commanded﴾, that is, proclaim openly the call to "There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God," and what you are commanded to explain and call to, or to warn against. ﴿And turn away from the polytheists﴾, and do not concern yourself with them.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, We suffice you against the mockers, who set up with God another god; but they are going to know﴾. The mockers referred to here, whose evil God promised to suffice His Messenger against, were al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, ʿAdi ibn Qays and al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth. All of them died within a short time from various afflictions, may the curse of God be upon them.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We know that your breast is constricted by what they say﴾, that is, because of their mockery and derision of you, and because of their extreme persistence in disbelief and obstinacy. So We guide you to what will ease your psychological pain: ﴿So exalt your Lord with His praise﴾, that is, say "Glory be to God and praise be to Him," and increase this remembrance. ﴿And be among those who prostrate﴾, that is, among those who pray, since prostration is only in prayer or in the recitation of the Qur'an. Therefore, when distressed, resort to prayer. This is why the Prophet ﷺ, whenever a matter grieved him, would turn to prayer.

His saying: ﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾, that is, persist in worship, which is obedience in utmost humility and submission to God, until there comes to you the certainty, which is death. For the grave is the first threshold of the Hereafter, and when a person dies and enters the Hereafter, his faith becomes pure certainty.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. The prohibition of disputing over the Book of God in the manner in which the People of the Book disputed.
2. The legitimacy of openly proclaiming the truth and explaining it, especially when there is no persecution.
3. The virtue of the formula "Glory be to God and praise be to Him." Whoever says it one hundred times, his sins will be forgiven, even if they were like the foam of the sea. This is related in the Sahih.
4. The legitimacy of the prayer of need (*salat al-hajah*). Whoever is afflicted by a matter or is distressed by it should pray a prayer through which God relieves what troubles him or fulfils his need, if He wills. He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.
